items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: A friend of mine, Andy Snitzer, wonderful saxophonist, also got a business degree.

ctx.x: Oh man, the inside stories. Well I’ve taken up enough of your time today and this has been really delightful. I’ll just wrap up with if you had a niece or nephew who felt that they wanted to pursue the jazz life, would you have any words of wisdom for them?

Well I would say that if it’s a calling do it. Like it was for me. And it is a calling for hundreds of young musicians. I do a lot of teaching at colleges and I’m in the presence of a lot of fabulous young musicians that are so into being a musician that that’s what they’re going to do by hook or by crook. And they’ll find their way one way or another by teaching, composing, and just playing. Others get a dual degree, you know, in business. That’s not a bad idea. A friend of mine, Andy Snitzer, wonderful…

social media thing. There’s an interesting article in this week’s New Yorker in fact I have it around, let me see I’ve got the title here. I just was trying to read it. It’s called, and it’s for younger people but it’s what’s happening, “So you want to be a Tik Tok star.” And it goes into the details of what’s actually going on in the current music business, none of which I have a clue about.
